Covenant Sign
KUV-uh-nunt SYN
noun phrase
From the Hebrew 'oth and Greek sphragis (seal); a visible token God appoints to mark, confirm, and seal His covenant promise.

📖 Biblical Definition

A covenant sign is a visible token that God Himself appoints to mark, confirm, and seal the promises of His covenant, distinguishing the sign from the thing it signifies. To Noah He gave the rainbow that He would no more destroy the earth by flood; to Abraham He gave circumcision as a seal of the righteousness of faith; to Israel He gave the Passover, that the destroying angel might pass over the blood-marked door. These signs neither create nor contain the grace they point to, yet they are not empty, for God binds His word to them and pledges Himself in them. Under the new covenant the signs are baptism and the Lord's Supper, the one sealing union with Christ in His death and resurrection, the other showing forth His broken body and shed blood till He come. The Reformed faith ever distinguishes the sign from the thing signified: the water is not the washing of the soul, nor the bread the very body, yet the believing recipient truly receives Christ and all His benefits by faith through the Spirit. Thus the sacraments are signs and seals of the covenant of grace, confirming the promise to the eye as the Word confirms it to the ear. They strengthen weak faith, mark the visible people of God, and direct the heart away from the token to the Christ it represents.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A visible token God appoints to mark and seal His covenant, distinct from the grace it signifies.

COVENANT SIGN, noun phrase. From the Hebrew 'oth and Greek sphragis, a visible seal God appoints to confirm His covenant.

A token divinely instituted, such as the rainbow, circumcision, the Passover, baptism, and the Lord's Supper.

The sign is ever distinguished from the thing signified, yet sacramentally united to it by God's word.

Of Abraham it is written in Romans 4:11 that he "received the sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of the faith."

A means whereby God confirms His promise to the eye, strengthening the faith of His people.

📖 Key Scripture

Rom 4:11 — "And he received the sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of the faith which he had yet being uncircumcised:"

Gen 9:13 — "I do set my bow in the cloud, and it shall be for a token of a covenant between me and the earth."

Gen 17:11 — "And ye shall circumcise the flesh of your foreskin; and it shall be a token of the covenant betwixt me and you."

Exo 12:13 — "And the blood shall be to you for a token upon the houses where ye are: and when I see the blood, I will pass over you."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Error gathers at both extremes—some make the sign empty ritual, others make it confer the grace it merely signifies.

expand to see more

Two opposite errors crowd around the covenant sign. The one empties it of meaning, treating baptism and the Supper as bare memorials or social customs with no abiding pledge of God. The other collapses the sign into the thing signified, so that the water is thought to wash the soul and the bread to become the very flesh of Christ—a confusion the Reformed faith firmly resists in distinguishing the seal from that which it seals.

To recover the truth we must hold the sign and the thing signified together yet distinct, as Scripture does. God truly pledges Himself in the appointed token, and the believing soul truly receives Christ by faith through the Spirit, yet the grace is not bound within the element nor conferred apart from faith. So the rainbow preached mercy, circumcision sealed righteousness by faith, and baptism and the Supper confirm the covenant of grace to the eye, ever pointing beyond themselves to Christ.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Covenant signs run through redemptive history as God's appointed seals of His sworn promise.

expand to see more

God Himself institutes the sign; man may not invent or alter it.

The sign is distinguished from the thing signified, yet united to it by God's word.

The rainbow, circumcision, and Passover were the chief signs under the old covenant.

Baptism and the Lord's Supper are the signs and seals of the new covenant.

The signs confirm the promise to the eye and direct faith to Christ alone.

Usage

"The church administers the covenant signs as God appointed them, neither despising nor over-valuing the elements."

"Pastors teach the people to look through the sign to the Christ it seals."

"The believer's faith is strengthened as the promise is confirmed to the eye in baptism and the Supper."
